title: East Zone One Day From Duleep Trophy Glory as Kishan Shines Again
excerpt: East Zone closed day four of the Duleep Trophy final at 212 for 5, a 584-run lead over South Zone, with Ishan Kishan's second-innings 80 following his 270 and leaving a first title in 14 years within reach.
body:
• East Zone reached 212 for 5 at stumps on day four of the Duleep Trophy final at Chepauk, a lead of 584 runs over South Zone.
  • Skipper Ishan Kishan followed his monumental 270 with 80 off 98 balls; No. 3 Shikhar Mohan contributed 52.
  • South Zone were bowled out for 336 in their first innings, 372 runs behind, with captain Tilak Varma falling one run short of a century on 99.
  • East are on the verge of a third Duleep Trophy title and their first in 14 years, after back-to-back wins in 2011/12 and 2012/13.

One hand on the trophy

East Zone are one day away from ending a 14-year wait. At stumps on day four of the Duleep Trophy final at Chennai's MA Chidambaram Stadium, East stood at 212 for 5 in their second innings — a lead of 584 runs that leaves South Zone chasing a near-impossible target on the final day. As The Hindu put it, East "does not give South an inch," and the coronation is now all but a matter of time.

https://x.com/BCCIdomestic/status/2097577398082691499

The day belonged once again to Ishan Kishan. Two days after his career-best 270 powered East to 708 — the third-highest total ever in a Duleep Trophy final — the East skipper produced a second act of 80 off 98 deliveries, striking nine fours and three sixes before falling. With his two innings at Chepauk, Kishan has carried East to the brink of only their third title in the competition's history.

"As The Hindu put it, East "does not give South an inch," and the coronation is now all but a matter of time."

South fold for 336

South Zone began the day at 242 for 6, still 466 behind East's mountain. They added another 94 in the morning session, built around a 78-run stand between Chama Milind, who made 43, and captain Tilak Varma. But Milind's dismissal opened the door, and South's resistance ended shortly after.

Mohammed Siraj held up one end as Tilak neared his ninth first-class hundred, but Siraj was the ninth batter to fall in the 107th over, and Tilak followed six balls later, lobbing a ball back to the bowler one run short of his century. Tilak's 99 was the standout effort of South's 336 — a first-innings deficit of 372 that made the second half of the day a formality.

It was a bitter end to a fine individual campaign for Tilak, whose red-ball form has been one of the stories of the tournament. After rescuing South in the semi-final against North Zone with an unbeaten 116 from 80 for 5 and then anchoring a 181-run chase with 51 not out, he now has three consecutive 50-plus scores in the competition. His first-class average sits above 58 across 24 matches.

Kishan doubles down

East lost Abhimanyu Easwaran and 15-year-old opener Vaibhav Sooryavanshi cheaply at the start of their second innings, but No. 3 Shikhar Mohan steadied the ship with 52 — his second fifty of the match — before Kishan took over again. The captain's 80 came at a strike rate that kept East's scoring rate racing along, and late counter-attacks from Kumar Kushagra and Zeeshan Ansari, who added an unbroken 50-run stand, carried East to stumps in full control.

The scale of Kishan's week is hard to overstate. His 270 — built with 30 fours and seven sixes after he retired hurt on 250 and returned to continue — is the second-highest individual score ever in a Duleep Trophy final, behind only Raman Lamba's 320 for North Zone in 1987. He became only the third East Zone batter to score a double century in the tournament's history, joining Arun Lal and Saba Karim. Along the way he brought up his 10th first-class hundred and crossed 4,000 first-class runs.

What's next

South face a final day with 585 runs to chase — an effectively impossible target — while a drawn game would hand East the title on first-innings lead. Either way, East stand one day from their third Duleep Trophy crown, after consecutive victories in 2011/12 and 2012/13.

For Kishan, the timing is significant. With India's selectors monitoring domestic performances ahead of upcoming international assignments, a 270 and 80 in a final — combined with the unbeaten knock that carried East past Central Zone in the semi-final — is about as loud a red-ball statement as a player can make.
